title: A check is not an approval
audience: A delivery team deciding whether to release
question: Can the team release the fictional Atlas update?
summary: The checks passed. Release approval is still pending. Keep the release on hold.
context: Fictional teaching example. Atlas, its records, and all events below are invented; no live system was checked or changed.

sources.title: Fictional Atlas validation record
sources.note: The defined checks passed for build A17 in the test environment. Production behavior was not tested.

sources.title: Fictional Atlas release decision record
sources.note: A release requires the release owner's recorded approval. That approval is pending; no decision date is recorded.

claims.text: The defined validation checks passed for build A17.
claims.scope: The test environment and defined checks only; not production readiness.

claims.text: The required release-owner approval is pending.
claims.uncertainty: The record supplies no approval date or eventual decision.

claims.text: Keep the release on hold and request the release owner's decision.
claims.scope: A proposed next step, not an approval or an executed action.

beats.title: Separate the evidence from the authority
beats.text: A passing check answers a bounded technical question. It does not grant the authority to release.

visual.title: Evidence reaches a gate — it does not open it
visual.description: The passed validation record is evidence for the release owner's decision. The required approval remains pending.
visual.caption: Fictional Atlas records. The arrow shows a review relationship, not an approval or automated release.

beats.title: Keep the gate visible
beats.text: Send the evidence to the release owner. Keep the release on hold while the required approval is pending.

question.prompt: A teammate says, “The checks passed, so we can release.” What is missing?
question.answer: The release owner's recorded approval. Passing checks provide evidence; they do not replace that decision.

limitations: This fictional brief proves nothing about a real build, organization, or release.
Source links and structural checks do not establish factual truth or adequate evidence.
No approval, deployment, API call, or model call is performed.
